notes: Scope: this family is context and practice, not an experiment family. Findings with "investigation": null are grouped by the prefix of "topic" (Exploration atmosphere, NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, Fire detection, Fire response, Suppression equipment, Incident ..., Communication delay, Partial gravity). All pillars are "response" or "design" as the task requires, including detection and suppression facts.

Investigation records: LUCI and FM2 only. PSI lists neither: psi-investigations.json (26 records) has no match for LUCI, FM2, "Lunar" or "partial gravity", so psi_id and psi_url are null. LUCI has 20 findings and FM2 has 22. LUCI "pi" is null: the 2025 presentation lists authors (Ferkul, Johnston, Kralik, Liao) but does not name a principal investigator. "flow" is null for both: neither source states a forced flow.

FM2 has not flown in any cached source, so every FM2 finding is a plan, a hypothesis, or ground and model evidence cited by the FM2 team. The carrier differs between NASA sources (CLPS mission CP-21 in the 2024 abstract; a SpaceX Human Lander System uncrewed test flight in the 2025 LUCI presentation, whose abstract also says "planned to launch in late 2026"). Both are recorded as separate findings.

Artemis II smoke alarm: the wording quoted by the challenge ("make the fire alarm go off in your spacecraft when you are still about 80,000 miles from home") was not found on nasa.gov. Tried the nasa.gov WordPress search API with 8 queries and the posts endpoint filtered to 2026 with 4 queries (no hit); the mission-blog API returned no JSON. The only cached text with it is the challenge page itself (raw/nasa/spaceapps-challenge-flame-in-freefall.txt, host spaceappschallenge.org, not one of the allowed NASA hosts), so no finding uses it. What nasa.gov does give is the post-flight NASA podcast episode 440 (fetched for this family as raw/nasa/podcast-to-the-moon-and-back-again.txt): the commander says the emergencies they had "pretty much turned out to be a false alarm" and describes the "first right thing" rule. Those are the Artemis II findings; none of them says the alarm was a smoke alarm.

Earth-Mars delay: the NASA sources give "up to 20 minutes one way" (HRP), four to 24 minutes one way (Goddard), "roundtrip ... up to 40 minutes" (Ames paper), 22-minute delays in the CHAPEA analog (direction not stated) and "up to 45 minutes each way" (CHAPEA one-year article). No cached NASA text states "22 minutes one way" or "44 minutes round trip"; the product tagline numbers should be shown as 20 one way / 40 round trip, or as the 4 to 24 minute range, with these sources.

Atmosphere numbers: the challenge page wording "30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psi or less" is not in a NASA source here. NASA sources give 10.2 psia/26.5% and 8.2 psia/34% (NESC 2026, M2M 2024), a possible maximum of 36 to 40% at 8.2 psia (NESC), materials testing at 37% (NESC bulletin), 30% at 10.2 psia as the ISS airlock and Shuttle worst case, and a 2007 proposal of 30% at 10.4 psia for the CEV (in raw/pdf/20070021223.txt, not used as a finding).

NASA-STD-6001: the quoted text of Test 1 is the 1998 edition (NTRS 19990036744, scanned, with OCR noise outside the quoted sentences). The active edition is NASA-STD-6001B with Change 3 (standards page cached, PDF not fetched), so the 6 in. (15 cm) criterion and sample size are stated as "1998 edition"; the 2014 NULP paper cached here still uses a 15.2 cm burn length criterion.

A tension the dashboard should show rather than hide: ISS, Shuttle and Orion procedures stop ventilation first and expect a fire to starve (OPERATIONS findings under "Fire response"), while the Researcher's Guide lists "a fire will self-extinguish if ventilation is shut off" among critical misconceptions and reports that a local suppressant jet can sustain a flame with ambient flow off. Both are quoted. Reading: ventilation shutdown is the right first step and is not proof of extinction.

Sources and kinds: NTRS records whose full text was cached from the PDF (files raw/nasa/ntrs-*.txt and raw/pdf/<id>.txt) are cited with kind "pdf" and the NTRS id, because their quotes are from the full text and would not pass a --refetch against the abstract. Kind "ntrs" is used only for quotes present in the record abstract (raw/ntrs/<id>.txt). Quotes from abstracts stop before the record markup (O<sub>2</sub>). Some PDF quotes keep a line-break hyphen or a bullet exactly as in the text (for example "100- 250 nm", "Water- Mist", "state-ofthe-art", "• Flame tip spread rate").

Files added for this family: raw/pdf/20250010653 (LUCI results), 20130010991 (Martian-gravity limits), 20250006779 (lunar ignition testing), 20210020516 (Fire on the Moon charts), each as .pdf and pdftotext .txt; raw/pdf/20070021223.pdf/.txt is the already cached CEV fire protection PDF re-extracted in reading order, because the cached two-column layout text interleaves columns; raw/nasa/podcast-to-the-moon-and-back-again.txt (+ html). No download of a source document failed.

Checks run on 2026-11-14: tools/quotecheck.py exits 0 on this file (264 of 264 quotes found verbatim in their cached text), and with --refetch all 47 quotes of kind "ntrs" were also found in the live NTRS title and abstract.

Not quoted on purpose: Table I of NTRS 20130010991 (limits per material and gravity level) is scrambled in the plain text extraction, so only its prose statements are used; the caption of its Figure 6 gives the average Martian margin as "2.7%" without the minus sign the text implies, and was left out. The Apollo 13 page says "carbon monoxide" where carbon dioxide removal is meant; that sentence was left out.

Conditions hold only values present in the cited source text (not always inside the quote itself). Evidence level "review or summary" is used for procedures, incident histories and program statements; "model or analysis" for the detection lumped model, the NESC assessment and CFD work; LUCI is marked "flight experiment" (suborbital rocket); drop-tower, centrifuge and aircraft work is "ground low-gravity".

findings.decision_hint: Keep fans off until extinction is confirmed.

findings.quote: If a location specific fire alarm is triggered, then power in that area is removed. This response is only performed within payload or system racks that are isolated from other areas within the spacecraft.

findings.decision_hint: Automate power removal for isolated equipment volumes on a local alarm.

findings.quote: With the material designs chosen to be non-flammable, by removing a constant ignition source, this response allows the fire to extinguish after the localized fuel is burned.

findings.decision_hint: This step only works if material control held; in a higher-oxygen cabin where more materials are flammable, do not assume burnout.

findings.quote: However, most ISS systems are behind closed panels, which can require a multi-step process to locate the fire.

findings.decision_hint: Give every closed equipment volume a labelled sampling and discharge port.

findings.quote: This case is a good example of how computer-based data and tools, or assistance from Mission Control, can greatly streamline and accelerate resolution actions.

findings.decision_hint: Where Mission Control cannot answer in time (Mars), the onboard tool has to carry this role alone.

findings.quote: If the fire extinguisher fails to stop the event, crew will proceed to a partial powerdown of the entire module they are located in, followed by a full powerdown and evacuation of the module.
